title: t19309: fix(headless): release the dispatch claim before the exit-trap terminal lease
body:
## Summary

_hrff_finalize_exit_trap emitted the worker runtime event before releasing the claim. Since GH#36553 that event posts this attempt's DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal, and dispatch-release-claim.jq then returns verdict terminal, so the following release was skipped ("no current unreleased matching dispatch claim"). Every prelaunch failure that exits through the EXIT trap (e.g. project_node_environment_failure) therefore left the issue assigned with status:in-progress until a peer's stale sweep reset it 12-30 min later, and two such resets trip the t2008 escalation to status:blocked + needs-ai-recovery. Observed 2026-11-23 on a private downstream repo: one device failed 33/33 dispatches in ~4 s each, posting only terminal leases and never CLAIM_RELEASED; five healthy issues were escalated within 30 minutes. The release now runs first (as _hrw_finish_not_launched and the normal finish path already do), so CLAIM_RELEASED with the prelaunch cause publishes and projects state immediately; the event's terminal lease remains the fallback. Dedup is unaffected: dispatch-lease-claims.jq maps a matching CLAIM_RELEASED to terminal attempt_id release, which _dd_has_matching_terminal_lease accepts. Also points a stale test assertion at headless-runtime-failure-classify.sh, where GH#37744 moved classify_worker_kill_reason (it failed on main).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-exited-kill-reason.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19309-brief.md

## Summary

title: GH#40059: fix(ci-wait): zero-check PRs return terminal no-checks instead of hanging

## Summary

GitHub returns commit.statusCheckRollup: null when a head has no check runs or statuses. The exact reader (_gh_pr_checks_exact_page_meta) rejected that as a partial/malformed page, so gh-checks-wait-helper retried until its 1800s timeout in both required and --all modes. The reader now accepts a null rollup on page 1 as a complete empty page (a rollup lost after page 1 stays fail-closed as partial). The waiter's fetch_checks now maps the mode-matched empty diagnostic ('no checks reported...' for --all, the existing required form otherwise) to []. Because an empty --all read can now reach classification, it holds the existing 90s settle window unless the repo is verified to have zero active workflows, so a fresh head cannot pass before its workflows register. The existing zero-check fixture now uses GitHub's real null shape. title: GH#40087: fix(buzz): bound ACP turns and delegate proxy runtime to the plugin
body:
## Summary

The Buzz plugin now enforces its declared 30-minute turn limit: an overdue session/prompt is cancelled via session/cancel, and if OpenCode has not ended it 60 s later the agent's ACP process is stopped and its sessions forgotten, so the queue moves on with a clear failure reply. With turns bounded, process-guard delegates runtime for the exact deployed `team-interface-acp-cwd-proxy.mjs --no-publish -- .../opencode-launcher-helper.sh remote-interactive` command line and its `opencode acp` child (owner `buzz-acp-plugin`). Arbitrary Node/OpenCode processes stay governed; RSS limits remain enforced. Plugin version 1.3.1.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/README.md, .agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/plugin.js, .agents/scripts/process-guard-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-process-guard-managed-workers.sh

## Decisions

Skipped the optional proxy signal rewording: the plugin's own acp.stop() also SIGTERMs the proxy, so attributing SIGTERM to a process guard would mislead. Local Node project validators were skipped (AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PROJECT_VALIDATORS=1) because they refuse any .agents/**/*.js change: .agents/package.json is a scriptless dependency manifest outside the root workspaces, so no package check owns plugin.js. No check that could run was skipped; CI gates apply. Follow-up issue filed for the validator gap.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Live: real Node processes with the exact proxy argv and a lookalike without --no-publish, scanned by this branch's process-guard-helper.sh scan with CHILD_RUNTIME_LIMIT=1: proxy => MANAGED 'runtime delegated to buzz-acp-plugin lifecycle controls'; lookalike => OVER_TIME. Not run: a >2h live Buzz soak.

Resolves #40087

title: t19325: fix(dispatch): size worker prelaunch lease to cover the canary bound
body:
## Summary

Pulse workers lost their dispatch lease when the model canary ran a real probe for longer than about 110 seconds, and then exited with `worker_ledger_ready_failed`. That is what happened to GH#40112's first attempt.

- The worker renewed its prelaunch claim for 120 s, but the canary that follows is bounded by `CANARY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (180 s). The ready transitions reject expired leases on both the GitHub claim and the local ledger, by design.
- The renewal did not extend `dispatch-ledger.jsonl` at all. The dispatcher's registration used the default 120 s prelaunch TTL.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-ownership.sh`: the new `_hrw_prelaunch_lease_ttl` returns the larger of the orphan grace and `CANARY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` + `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_PRELAUNCH_ALLOWANCE_SECONDS`, which is 300 s by default. The renewal passes it to the GitHub claim transition, then makes a best-effort ledger renewal with the same TTL. This follows manual dispatch, which already sizes its lease from the canary timeout (`_dsi_renew_prelaunch_lease`).
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-ledger-helper.sh`: new `renew` command. It extends only an active `prelaunch` lease for the matching token, never shortens it, never turns a `ready` lease back into `prelaunch`, and never revives an expired lease. The strict expiry checks on `ready` are unchanged.

## Evidence

- GH#40112 attempt `attempt:789867d0`: the ledger lease expired at 00:20:40Z; the canary ran from 00:18:51Z to 00:21:24Z (153 s); `ready` ran at about 00:21:35Z, giving `worker_ledger_ready_failed`.
- Across 1,182 retained worker logs, the renewal-to-ready gap has a median of 7 s and a p90 of 13 s, with a maximum of 165 s (this attempt). It is rare, but it clusters when providers are slow.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` is clean on both files, and the pre-commit ratchets pass.
- An ad-hoc runtime check against a temporary ledger passed 12 of 12 cases: extends, keeps prelaunch, a shorter renewal is a no-op that appends nothing, a wrong token is denied, ready follows renewal, a ready lease cannot be downgraded, an expired lease is not revived, a missing entry is denied.
- `_hrw_prelaunch_lease_ttl`: default 300 s; 162 s with a 42 s canary; falls back on invalid input; never drops below the orphan-grace floor.
- Existing suites pass: `tests/test-dispatch-ledger-helper.sh`, `tests/test-dispatch-atomic-lease.sh`, `tests/test-worker-warm-start-opencode.sh`.

## Cost

A worker that dies during prelaunch holds its dedup lease for up to 300 s instead of 120 s.

Resolves #40118

title: t19324: runner-local dispatch lock behind PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT
body:
## Summary

Adds a runner-local dispatch lock (LOCKDIR.dispatch, override PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCKDIR) separate from the Pulse instance lock, behind PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT (default 0). With the flag on, every dispatch round (early_dispatch, post_label_refill, cycle_dispatch_max, active-pulse refill, early_exit_recycle_fill, cycle_final_refill, event_refill_drain) takes the dispatch lock, so rounds never overlap, and a refill-only run no longer waits for the instance lock held through maintenance stages. Each acquire logs the owner PID (BASHPID-resolved, so subshell rounds record their real PID). Stale reclaim covers a dead owner, PID reuse by a non-pulse command, and a heartbeat older than PULSE_LOCK_MAX_AGE_S; the instance-lock heartbeat also refreshes the dispatch heartbeat. The lock is re-entrant, release is owner-checked, and it is released on EXIT before the instance lock and before the exec path. Refill-only runs without the env var follow the mode published by the latest cycle (LOCKDIR.dispatch-mode). With the flag off, nothing changes: every wrapper falls through to a direct call, and refill keeps the instance lock, the GH#35349 cooldown and the refill budget. Old refill layers are kept (Phase 3 follow-up). Rollout: merge with the flag off; enable on one runner via its launchd/systemd environment and compare pulse-throughput-report-helper.sh output (#40109) for 6 h before and after; making it the default is a follow-up.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-instance-lock.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh

## Decisions

Shared-state audit (flag on). (1) Candidate census and handoff: MOVED. Invalidation in post_label_refill, Phase 2 consolidation and triage enumeration runs inside dispatch rounds, and the refill census hand-off runs under the dispatch lock. Cycle EXIT cleanup still runs outside it but is SAFE: the hand-off is mktemp+mv atomic, removals only force a re-scan, and live claim/ledger gates still arbitrate every candidate. (2) Worktree cleanup vs dedup precreate_worktree: SAFE. The owner PID is recorded at precreate (pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh), cleanup checks _worktree_owner_alive, and orphans get a 1800 s grace. (3) cleanup_stale_opencode vs a just-spawned worker: SAFE. It prunes caches and scratch only and never kills workers (pulse-cleanup.sh). (4) Ownership and assignment reconcile: SAFE. _preflight_ownership_reconcile writes no ledger, PID or claim files. dispatch-ledger cmd_expire holds the ledger lock and expires only dead-PID, PID-reuse or lease-expired entries, while in-flight prelaunch claims renew their lease. stale_queued_runs only cancels queued GitHub Actions runs. normalize_active_issue_assignments keeps its existing 600 s updatedAt guard on unassign. (5) Slot accounting: MOVED. Throttle-file writers and base-parallel compute run inside apply_dispatch_max rounds, now serialized; active-worker counts read live processes. (6) Stats read-modify-write: SAFE. pulse_stats_increment serializes on its own stats lock with temp+mv writes. The two-live-workers-per-issue guarantee still rests on the existing dispatch claim/ledger dedup, which this change does not weaken; with the flag on, rounds no longer overlap at all.

- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Acceptance suites pass on the rebased branch: test-pulse-event-refill (39/39), test-dispatch-max-parallel, test-pulse-cycle-state-contract, test-pulse-wrapper-characterization (54/54), test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape. Independent copies of the same real recovery store, identical initial cursors, 45-second `pending --count` budgets; no profiling writes targeted the live recovery store. Only aggregate counts are reported.
